title: REPORT on the implementation of Europe’s Beating Cancer Plan
part_text: Text as a whole without the words: ‘particularly’ and ‘stresses the need for targeted and evidence-based measures to close regulatory gaps in current marketing and advertising practices while further looking into the impact of harmful alcohol consumption, particularly at levels exceeding scientifically established health recommendations, energy drinks and so-called ultra-processed foods on people’s health;’
part_context: Highlights that 40 %[[43]](#footnote-44) of cancers are preventable and that achieving targets on cancer prevention, including by implementing measures to reduce exposure to risk factors such as tobacco, harmful alcohol consumption, <del>particularly</del> at levels exceeding scientifically established health recommendations, an unhealthy diet, environmental contaminants, air pollutants and exposure to harmful materials and substances, such as carcinogenic, mutagenic and reprotoxic substances and endocrine disruptors, are complementary to efforts to prevent other non-communicable diseases; stresses the need for targeted and evidence-based measures to close regulatory gaps in current marketing and advertising practices while further looking into the impact of harmful alcohol consumption, particularly at levels exceeding scientifically established health recommendations, energy drinks and so-called ultra-processed foods on people’s health;
